items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Well, I played with a fellow named Bill Phillips. He's a drummer.

ctx.x: What kind of a band did you have there or did you play with in your first jobs?

Well, I played with a fellow named Bill Phillips. He's a drummer. He's still around there. But I never will forget my first job. I played on Mardi Gras there on the truck. I could play three songs. The Sheik of Araby, I Love You, and some other rhythm song. I can't remember what that one was. But we got up in the Irish Channel and a fellow called me off on the side. He said, look here, fellow. He says, can't you play anything with those three songs?
He's been following you around, huh?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Bill Phillips came to get me to play with his band and my professor didn't think that I should play in a band

ctx.x: This is Kenneth. Is he here? He's here, but he's over at his house with his wife. I believe Bill met him. Yes. He came in just as Bill was completing the interview. And he is 31 years old now. Did he play anything? No, he never did want music. Now we'll get back to Bill Phillips. That is the first band that I actually played with and he was the cause that my professor stopped teaching me. Bill Phillips came to get me to play with his band and my professor didn't think that I should play in a band but he had never…
Was Milford Piron akin to AJ?
